questions.question: Which is the world's largest coral reef system?
questions.hint: The Great Barrier Reef stretches over 2,300 km along Australia's northeast coast and is the largest coral reef system on Earth.

questions.question: Which bird has the largest wingspan of any living bird?
questions.hint: The Wandering Albatross can have a wingspan exceeding 3.5 meters (11.5 feet).

questions.question: Which movie became the first ever to earn over $2 billion at the worldwide box office?
questions.hint: James Cameron's Avatar (2009) was the first film to surpass $2 billion globally.

questions.question: In Harry Potter, what is the name of the prison guarded by Dementors?
questions.hint: Azkaban is the high-security wizard prison in the Harry Potter universe.

questions.question: Which international court settles legal disputes between countries?
questions.hint: The ICJ is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations.

questions.question: Which document established the United Nations in 1945?
questions.hint: The UN Charter serves as the founding treaty of the United Nations.

questions.question: Which civilization is credited with building the pyramids at Giza?
questions.hint: The Great Pyramids were built as royal tombs during Egypt's Old Kingdom.

questions.question: Which famous document was signed in England in 1215, limiting the king's powers?
questions.hint: The Magna Carta laid the foundation for constitutional government and the rule of law.

questions.question: Which sport awards the Stanley Cup?
questions.hint: The Stanley Cup is the championship trophy of the NHL.

questions.question: How many points is a touchdown worth in American football before the extra point attempt?
questions.hint: A touchdown is worth six points, followed by an optional extra-point or two-point conversion.

questions.question: Which country has the greatest number of time zones?
questions.hint: Including its overseas territories, France spans 12 official time zones—the most of any country.

questions.question: Which mountain range separates Europe and Asia?
questions.hint: The Ural Mountains are traditionally considered part of the boundary between Europe and Asia.

questions.question: Which particle carries a negative electric charge?
questions.hint: Electrons orbit the nucleus and carry a negative elementary charge.

questions.question: Which planet has the largest number of confirmed moons?
questions.hint: Saturn currently holds the record for the highest number of confirmed natural satellites.

questions.question: Which country is famous for originating the martial art of Taekwondo?
questions.hint: Taekwondo is South Korea's national martial art and an Olympic sport.

questions.question: Which instrument traditionally has 88 keys?
questions.hint: A standard modern piano contains 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black.

questions.question: Which is the largest species of penguin?
questions.hint: Emperor Penguins can reach about 1.2 meters (4 feet) in height.

questions.question: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.hint: Lesotho is one of only three enclave countries in the world and is entirely surrounded by South Africa.

questions.question: Which branch of science studies fungi?
questions.hint: Mycology is the scientific study of fungi, including mushrooms, molds, and yeasts.

questions.question: Which explorer completed the first successful circumnavigation of the Earth, although he died before the voyage ended?
questions.hint: Magellan led the expedition that first circumnavigated the globe. He was killed in the Philippines in 1521, and his crew completed the journey in 1522.
